subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 55 years old, male, and I'm here because I've been having some back pain. It started about five days ago when I was helping my wife move a refrigerator and felt something in my lower right back. I'm just worried that maybe something happened, especially since I had a discectomy before. Doctor: Can you describe the nature of the back pain, whether it radiates to other areas, and if you have any associated symptoms such as numbness, tingling, or weakness in your legs? Patient: The pain is in my lower right back, and it hurts when I bend over. I haven't had any numbness, tingling, or weakness in my legs, just the pain in my back. Doctor: Could you describe the intensity of the pain on a scale from 1 to 10, and have you noticed any specific activities or positions that make the pain better or worse? Patient: The pain is a 6 or 7 out of 10. It feels worse when I bend over or try to move the way I did when I hurt it, but it doesn't get better much when I rest. Just the pain in my back, nothing else. Doctor: Could you describe any specific activities or movements that make the pain better or worse? Also, have you tried any treatments or interventions for the previous discectomy that might be relevant here? Patient: The pain is worse when I bend over or try to move the way I did when I hurt it, but it doesn't get better much when I rest. I've been taking ibuprofen and once tried Tylenol and ibuprofen together, which gave me some relief. I had a discectomy before, but I don't know if that's related to this. Doctor: Could you describe the specific location of the tenderness in your lower back and whether there is any radiating pain? Additionally, have you noticed any changes in your bowel or bladder function since the onset of the pain? Patient: The tenderness
